seed: Objects of type `marker` under action ACTION4 with touching neighbours [hazard,wall] show mixed outcomes: no_change x2, x x1. Find the condition in the before state that decides the outcome. Start from this kind of condition: a global object such as a counter, HUD element or legend, read as state. Verify it against every transition before you keep it.

synth.notes:
Blocks (colour 10) move in mirrored 4-cell steps: A1 up, A2 down, A3 apart, A4 together. A move happens only if the 4x4 destination is all floor colour 5 within rows 1-62.
Clicking colour 9 arms that marker (blocks turn colour 1, the marker turns 11, the old active marker reverts to 9). Clicking colour 1 disarms. Any other click does nothing.
While armed, A1-A4 move the active marker cell under the same floor rule. A5 does nothing but still counts as an action.
HUD: a row of 0s along row 0 (from the right) and row 63 (from the left), width 3(a+1)//7, a = actions this level. a is carried only while the frame is continuous; 13/30 without it.
The hinted marker A4 global-counter condition is a red herring: the outcome depends only on the colour of the destination cell. Unconfirmed: HUD behaviour beyond 9 bar cells.
